newsitem.title: HUNGARY: EGIS H1 SALES RISE ON STRONGER EXPORT.
newsitem.headline: EGIS H1 SALES RISE ON STRONGER EXPORT.

text.p: Hungarian pharmaceuticals company Egis Gyogyszergyar Rt reported its overall sales rising 8.5 percent in the first half of 1997 as higher exports more than offset falling domestic sales.
"In Egis Rt's operations between April and June 1997, the trends of the first quarter continued," Egis said in its earnings report on Monday.
"Domestic sales remained below targets set for the period, while exports grew dynamically in harmony with plans."

Egis, majority owned by France's Servier SA, reported its after-tax profits falling to 3.033 billion forints in the first six months of 1997 from 3.314 billion in the first half of 1996 while its net sales rose to 13.593 billion from 12.529 billion.
Domestic sales fell to 6.422 billion forints from 7.289 billion, while exports grew 7.171 billion forints from 5.240 billion.

"Exports amounted to $20.7 million between April and June, and to $40.6 million between January and June 30," Egis said. "This represents a rise of 13 percent in dollar terms over exports in the first half of the previous year."
Egis added that exports to the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) and exports of active ingredients grew the fastest, by 26 percent and 23 percent respectively in dollar terms.
The company added that in the first half of the year it invested 2.637 billion forints.
